results.name: parity_match_outside_span_gap
results.description: In sets of >=2 whose examples all share a parity, yes-rate for targets outside the span with the same parity minus opposite parity; observed above null means people use the parity rule beyond the range more than the model (which favors ranges), below null means the model over-weights parity rules.
results.code:
# name: parity_match_outside_span_gap
# description: In sets of >=2 whose examples all share a parity, yes-rate for targets outside the span with the same parity minus opposite parity; observed above null means people use the parity rule beyond the range more than the model (which favors ranges), below null means the model over-weights parity rules.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    last = X[np.arange(len(X)), n - 1]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    par = np.where(np.isnan(X), np.nan, np.mod(X, 2))
    allsame = (np.nanmax(par, axis=1) == np.nanmin(par, axis=1))
    sp = np.nanmin(par, axis=1)
    out = (t < mn) | (t > mx)
    g = (n >= 2) & allsame & out
    same = g & (np.mod(t, 2) == sp)
    diff = g & (np.mod(t, 2) != sp)
    if same.sum() == 0 or diff.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[same].mean() - r[diff].mean())

results.name: lag1_response_autocorr
results.description: Within-session lag-1 correlation of consecutive yes/no responses (consecutive trial_index); observed above null means responses perseverate (or drift in runs) beyond what the stimulus-driven model reproduces, below null means people alternate more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: lag1_response_autocorr
# description: Within-session lag-1 correlation of consecutive yes/no responses (consecutive trial_index); observed above null means responses perseverate (or drift in runs) beyond what the stimulus-driven model reproduces, below null means people alternate more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    last = X[np.arange(len(X)), n - 1]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(int).values
    ok = np.diff(ti) == 1
    a = r[:-1][ok]
    b = r[1:][ok]
    if len(a) < 3 or a.std() == 0 or b.std() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1])

results.name: singleton_same_decade_gap
results.description: For single-example sets, among non-example targets within 9 of the example, yes-rate for targets in the same decade (same (x-1)//10) minus a different decade; observed above null means people use decade boundaries more strongly than the model's decade bonus, below null means the model over-weights decade-aligned ranges.
results.code:
# name: singleton_same_decade_gap
# description: For single-example sets, among non-example targets within 9 of the example, yes-rate for targets in the same decade (same (x-1)//10) minus a different decade; observed above null means people use decade boundaries more strongly than the model's decade bonus, below null means the model over-weights decade-aligned ranges.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    last = X[np.arange(len(X)), n - 1]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    x = X[:, 0]
    near = (n == 1) & (np.abs(t - x) <= 9) & (t != x)
    sd = (t - 1) // 10 == (x - 1) // 10
    a = near & sd
    b = near & ~sd
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: outside_gradient_steepness
results.description: In sets of >=2, yes-rate for targets 1-3 outside the example span minus yes-rate for targets 7-12 outside the span (either side); observed above null means people's generalization falls off more steeply just beyond the edges than the model predicts, below null means a shallower gradient than the model.
results.code:
# name: outside_gradient_steepness
# description: In sets of >=2, yes-rate for targets 1-3 outside the example span minus yes-rate for targets 7-12 outside the span (either side); observed above null means people's generalization falls off more steeply just beyond the edges than the model predicts, below null means a shallower gradient than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    last = X[np.arange(len(X)), n - 1]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    g = n >= 2
    a = g & (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 3)
    b = g & (dist >= 7) & (dist <= 12)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: round_target_outside_gap
results.description: Among targets outside the example span (all sets) whose example set contains no multiple of 10, yes-rate for round targets (multiples of 10) minus non-round targets; observed above null means people favour round numbers beyond what the model's rules/decade ranges produce, below null means the model over-credits round targets.
results.code:
# name: round_target_outside_gap
# description: Among targets outside the example span (all sets) whose example set contains no multiple of 10, yes-rate for round targets (multiples of 10) minus non-round targets; observed above null means people favour round numbers beyond what the model's rules/decade ranges produce, below null means the model over-credits round targets.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    last = X[np.arange(len(X)), n - 1]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    has10 = (np.mod(np.nan_to_num(X, nan=1.0), 10) == 0).any(axis=1)
    out = ((t < mn) | (t > mx)) & ~has10
    a = out & (t % 10 == 0)
    b = out & (t % 10 != 0)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: above_below_asym_max_not_last
results.description: In sets of >=2 whose largest example is NOT shown last, yes-rate for targets 1-10 above the max minus yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the min; the model gives these sets no top credit (symmetric size-principle extension), so observed below null means people still restrict upward extension without the max-last cue, above null means they extend upward more than the model.
results.code:
# name: above_below_asym_max_not_last
# description: In sets of >=2 whose largest example is NOT shown last, yes-rate for targets 1-10 above the max minus yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the min; the model gives these sets no top credit (symmetric size-principle extension), so observed below null means people still restrict upward extension without the max-last cue, above null means they extend upward more than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    last = X[np.arange(len(X)), n - 1]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    g = (n >= 2) & (last != mx)
    up = g & (t > mx) & (t <= mx + 10)
    dn = g & (t < mn) & (t >= mn - 10)
    if up.sum() == 0 or dn.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[up].mean() - r[dn].mean())

results.name: far_outside_span_yes
results.description: Yes-rate for targets more than 20 away from the nearest edge of the example span (sets of >=2); observed above null means people generalize far beyond the examples (broad rule-like concepts) more than the model predicts, below null means the model over-produces far generalization.

def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    last = X[np.arange(len(X)), n - 1]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    m = (n >= 2) & (dist > 20)

results.name: inside_span_width_corr
results.description: Correlation between example-span width (max-min) and yes response for non-example targets strictly inside the span (sets of >=2); observed below null means people reject interior gaps of wide spans more than the model (they distrust wide ranges / fall back on rules), above null means they fill wide spans more readily than the model.
results.code:
# name: inside_span_width_corr
# description: Correlation between example-span width (max-min) and yes response for non-example targets strictly inside the span (sets of >=2); observed below null means people reject interior gaps of wide spans more than the model (they distrust wide ranges / fall back on rules), above null means they fill wide spans more readily than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    last = X[np.arange(len(X)), n - 1]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & (t > mn) & (t < mx) & ~is_ex
    w = (mx - mn)[m]
    y = r[m]
    if m.sum() < 3 or w.std() == 0 or y.std() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(w, y)[0, 1])
